Another of them included discourses with "I am" sayings between seven signs, or miracles, culminating in the raising of Lazarus. Besides the naming the Carmelite author of The Dark Night of the Soul, this name is given to an author who described the Seven Churches of Asia and the Whore of Babylon. text: This book's sixth chapter contains a much debated section in which the author claims it is impossible for the once enlightened to be brought back if they fall away. It uses a famous athletic analogy in urging readers to "run with perseverance the race marked out for us" and to "fix our eyes on Jesus, the author and perfecter of our faith." This book's eleventh chapter begins with the note that "faith is being sure of what we hope for and certain of what we do not see" and presents a "Faith Hall of Fame" of people like Noah. In its seventh chapter, it uses the figure of "Melchizedek" as an example of someone who is both priest and king. This book's first chapters stress Jesus' superiority to the angels, the high priests, and prophets like Moses. Unlike the other epistles, its author does not identify himself. For 10 points, name this New Testament epistle directed to the title audience of Jewish Christians.

The Sumerian God associated with this fathered Ishtar and Shamash by his wife Ningal, and he was named Nanna.
